Hi Camila —

1) Migration guardrail: when Redwood upgrades a model (for example 13B -> 70B) we need a defined transition price path for 90 days so monthly spend doesn't spike. Can you add language for a temporary migration rate cap or a smoothing credit?

4) Definition of billable unit: we need the token/embedding mapping spelled out (prompt vs completion vs special system tokens).

I attached the procurement markup (OrderForm_ExhibitD_redline_v1.pdf) with inline comments. If helpful we can jump on a short call to walk through.

message_2:
From: camila_reyes@redwood.ai

Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 9 Nov 2027 10:15:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Exhibit D questions + migration guardrail request

Marta —

Thanks for the clear markup — that helps. I pulled together proposed redlines and rationale below and attached a clean redline PDF plus an XLS pricing table that maps the monthly bands to unit definitions. High level responses first:

1) Migration guardrail: we can add a 90-day "migration smoothing" provision. Proposed language: "If Redwood upgrades the model serving Customers' routed requests to a higher resource model family, Redwood will apply a migration smoothing credit for the first 90 days equivalent to the difference between the historical weighted average unit price and the new unit price, capped at 20% of the customer's monthly committed spend." This preserves predictability while allowing us to recover costs.

2) Cap vs floor on true-ups: we are amenable to an invoice floor to avoid single-month cliffs. Suggested: "Monthly invoice true-ups will be subject to a minimum reconciliation floor equal to 50% of the customer's monthly committed spend for the applicable period, with the annual true-up recalculated at contract year-end."

3) Stair-step retroactivity: retroactive application is unusual for our template because it materially changes month-over-month forecasting for shared capacity pools. As a compromise we propose a pro-rated retroactive credit if the band is reached and sustained for the remainder of the calendar month (not for single-day spikes). Language: "If the higher discount band is achieved and maintained for the remainder of the calendar month, Redwood will apply a pro-rated retroactive credit for the portion of the month prior to the band attainment."

4) Billable unit definition: attached pricing_schedule_table.xlsx enumerates prompt/completion/system tokens and embedding units. We'll add a short definitions table to Exhibit D and reference the runtime tokenization doc.

See attached: OrderForm_ExhibitD_redline_v2.pdf (our edits) and pricing_schedule_table.xlsx.

Next steps: I copied Ben and Karthik to validate the economics and legal wording. If these look OK to you, we can incorporate into the MPA and route to DocuSign. If you prefer, let's do a 30-minute call Wednesday morning PST.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Director, GTM Contracts & Pricing
Redwood Inference

Attachments: OrderForm_ExhibitD_redline_v2.pdf; pricing_schedule_table.xlsx
